## Appearance

Diana Barry is characterized by her glossy, jet-black curls and expressive black eyes. She has a rosy, crimson complexion with dimples and a plump, dimpled hand.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER VIII. Anne’s Bringing-up Is Begun P40](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0040), [v1 CHAPTER XV. ## Personality

Diana is a good, smart, and ladylike individual with a practical nature, alongside an unselfish admiration for the talents of her friends. She possesses a skill for singing, notably demonstrated by performing solos. Additionally, she is known for her splendid ability to make lettuce salad and holds a reputation for her notable taste in dressing.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER VIII. Anne’s Bringing-up Is Begun P40](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0040), [v1 CHAPTER XV. ## History

Diana Barry was named by a schoolmaster who boarded with her family when she was born. In her youth, she met [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) in the garden at [Orchard Slope](../codex/places.md#orchard-slope), where they solemnly vowed eternal friendship. Their bond faced an early test when Mrs. [Barry](../character/barry.md) temporarily forbade Diana from playing with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), but Diana later rushed to [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) for help when her sister [Minnie May](../character/minnie-may.md) fell ill with severe croup. After [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) successfully treated [Minnie May](../character/minnie-may.md), Diana's mother restored the girls' friendship in gratitude. As their school years progressed, Diana gave [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) [Christmas](../codex/places.md#merry-christmas) gifts, formed a story club with her, and excitedly brought the newspaper to [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) announcing Anne's top score on the entrance exams. She actively joined [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) in community affairs, canvassing for the [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) Village [Improvement Society](../codex/factions.md#improvers), accompanying [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) on outings, and aiding in hosting special guests. When [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) departed for [Redmond College](../codex/places.md#redmond-college), Diana expressed deep concern about her leaving, though the two maintained their close connection during holidays and summer breaks. Diana read and gave feedback on Anne's writing, and later confided her engagement to [Fred Wright](../character/fred-wright.md). [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) helped Diana prepare for her wedding, where they fondly remembered their childhood vows before Diana married [Fred](../character/fred-wright.md). Eventually, Diana welcomed a newborn baby, which [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) came to visit.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER II. Matthew Cuthbert Is Surprised P64](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0064), [v1 CHAPTER XII. ## Quotes

> "I’m awfully glad you’ve come to live at Green Gables. It will be jolly to have somebody to play with. There isn’t any other girl who lives near enough to play with, and I’ve no sisters big enough."
>
> — Diana Barry — [v1 CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise P27](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0027)

> “Yes,” said Diana, tossing her head, “but I’m sure he doesn’t like Julia Bell so very much. I’ve heard him say he studied the multiplication table by her freckles.”
>
> — Diana Barry — [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P19](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0019)

> “Those Pye girls are cheats all round,” said Diana indignantly, as they climbed the fence of the main road. “Gertie Pye actually went and put her milk bottle in my place in the brook yesterday. Did you ever? I don’t speak to her now.”
>
> — Diana Barry — [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P26](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0026)

> “I don’t believe he’ll find the doctor at Carmody,” sobbed Diana. “I know that Dr. Blair went to town and I guess Dr. Spencer would go too. Young Mary Joe never saw anybody with croup and Mrs. Lynde is away. Oh, Anne!”
>
> — Diana Barry — [v1 CHAPTER XVIII. Anne to the Rescue P24](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0024)

> “Everything went off very well,” said Diana practically. “I guess we must have made as much as ten dollars. Mind you, Mr. Allan is going to send an account of it to the Charlottetown papers.”
>
> — Diana Barry — [v1 CHAPTER XXV. Matthew Insists on Puffed Sleeves P49](../source/v01-c25.md#nw-v01-c25-p0049)

## Relationships

### [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--diana-barry.md)

Diana and [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) became close friends after meeting in the garden at [Orchard Slope](../codex/places.md#orchard-slope) and solemnly swearing eternal friendship. They later served together as committee members for the [Improvement Society](../codex/factions.md#improvers). Their bond has survived various trials, such as when Diana rushed to [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) for Anne's help in treating her sister's severe croup, or when Diana assisted [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) in preparing for performances.
